Floors Tony coats

Garage floors with decorative flake

Flake is the usual pick for a garage. Chips go into the color coat, and a clear top coat seals them in.

Solid color epoxy

One even color from wall to wall, for a clean, plain floor.

Metallic epoxy

A swirled, glossy finish. Every metallic floor comes out a little different.

Shop and commercial floors

For shops and work bays, a solid color is the plain choice. Tell Tony what goes on the floor day to day and he'll help you pick.

Basement floors

Coated concrete is easier to sweep and mop than a bare slab. Solid color and metallic finishes both work down there.

Ask about a basement floor

Concrete prep and crack repair

A coating is only as good as the slab under it. Ask Tony how he would prep yours and fix the cracks before anything goes on top.

Ask Tony about colors

How a floor job goes

  1. Call

    Call Tony or send the form below. Tell him about the floor and what it gets used for.

  2. Pick

    Look through the finishes, then settle on colors with Tony before the job starts.

  3. Prep

    Talk the slab through with Tony, including any cracks that need repair before the coating.

  4. Coat

    Then the floor gets its coat. On a flake floor, a clear top coat seals the chips in.

Quick answers

For anything else, call Tony at (302) 747-4736.

Do you work in my area?

Call (302) 747-4736 with your address. Tony will tell you if he can take the job.

Which finish suits a garage?

Flake is the usual pick for a garage because the chips hide dust and marks. For a plainer look, a solid color works too.

Can you fix the cracks in my slab first?

Yes, crack repair is one of the jobs Tony does. Ask him how he would prep your slab.

Do you coat shop and commercial floors?

Yes. Call Tony with the size of the space and what goes on the floor, and he'll talk you through the options.

Are the finishes on this page photos?

No. They're drawn so you can compare the kinds of finish. Ask about real colors when you call.
